name: StubHub Holdings, Inc.

profile.description: StubHub is a leading global secondary marketplace for live-event tickets. It was formed when viagogo, founded by CEO Eric Baker, acquired StubHub in February 2020. Q2 2026 revenue rose 33% to $573.1M on record GMS of $3.1B (+34%), helped by FIFA World Cup demand, and management raised full-year 2026 GMS guidance to $10.1-10.3B. FY2025 showed a $1.9B net loss driven by IPO-related charges. Baker controls more than 50% of the voting power, making StubHub a controlled company. Market cap approximately $2.2B at $5.78, down from a 52-week high of $19.87.

innovation.label: DEVELOPING
innovation.analysis: Track Record (1/3): The main transformation in the last five years is the viagogo-StubHub combination and the post-COVID rebuild, from $35.6M of revenue in pandemic-hit FY2020 to $1.75B in FY2025. That is a business recovery rather than a new product category [3]. AI Deployment (1/2): StubHub is pushing AI across the organization, including customer-facing chatbots that its 10-Q flags as a risk, but reports no quantified AI savings or revenue; Glassdoor reviewers describe a push for 'AI in everything to a point of diminishing quality' [4][5]. Market Share (2/2): A category leader in secondary ticketing, with record Q2 2026 GMS of $3.1B (+34%) and full-year GMS guidance of $10.1-10.3B [1][6]. Pipeline (1/2): Growth initiatives such as direct issuance and major-event demand are discussed, but without specific product timelines [6]. R&D Intensity (0/1): No separate R&D line is disclosed in FMP data; technology spend is bundled into operating expenses [3].

inspiration.label: WEAK
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (2/4): StubHub's filings describe a marketplace purpose of connecting fans with live events and call its culture 'a critical component to our success', which is clear but not distinctive [4]. Community Impact (0/2): No distinctive charitable programs found. In April 2026 StubHub paid $10M to settle FTC allegations that it 'publicly supported the FTC's fees rule while privately planning to violate it' [7]. Employee Retention (0/2): Glassdoor rates StubHub 2.4/5 across 802 reviews with only 24% CEO approval, and reviewers cite 'high turnover and loss of strong performers' [5]. Insider Buying (0/2): No net insider buying found; the founder-CEO's control comes from super-voting shares [4].

infrastructure.label: DEVELOPING
infrastructure.analysis: Mechanically scored on 6 available metrics (8 units). These score 1.0: D/E of 67.2% (just under the 70% target), revenue growth of 33.2% YoY, a forward P/E of 9.5, and the revenue CAGR at 2x weight [2]. For the CAGR we used the 4-year FY2021-FY2025 figure of 26.9% (derived from FMP), because the FY2020 COVID base of $35.6M would distort a 5-year figure [3]. ROE of -102.9% (2x) and the profit margin of -91.3% both score 0.0, reflecting the $1.9B FY2025 net loss tied to IPO-related charges [2][3]. No provider PEG is available (negative trailing EPS), so it is excluded. Weighted 5.0/8 = 6. Liquidity: 6.06M x $5.78 = ~$35.0M/day.

ai_resilience.label: MODERATE
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (6/9): StubHub's moat is two-sided marketplace liquidity (buyers and resellers) and its guarantee/fulfilment trust layer, which AI tools cannot easily replicate. Live-event attendance is inherently physical [1][4]. The risks are AI shopping agents that aggregate prices across marketplaces and squeeze take rates, and AI-enabled bots, so the company sits in the PROTECTED tier rather than higher. AI Opportunity (0/1): No AI-derived revenue is disclosed.

infinite_game.summary: Through Sinek's lens, StubHub plays a largely finite game. Its competitive posture is adversarial toward primary ticketing incumbents, the FTC fee case points to tactical rule-bending, and employee sentiment (2.4/5 Glassdoor, 24% CEO approval) suggests low trust [5][7]. Founder Eric Baker deserves credit for persistence: he held the business together after buying StubHub weeks before COVID shut down live events, when FY2020 revenue fell to $35.6M [3][4].

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (1/3): Connecting fans with live experiences could support a real cause. In practice, the company's identity and public controversies center on fees and resale economics rather than a purpose that guides strategic sacrifice [4][7].

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (0/2): Glassdoor 2.4/5 (802 reviews), 24% CEO approval, and reviewer comments about a 'lack of trust in leadership' and high turnover point to a weak Circle of Safety [5].

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): StubHub frames the ticketing market as a battle against entrenched primary players and regulators rather than a source of learning. The FTC alleged it privately planned to violate a rule it publicly supported [7].

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): StubHub survived a near-total revenue collapse in 2020 and rebuilt to $1.75B by FY2025, and it is expanding into direct issuance alongside resale [3][6]. These are adaptations of its core marketplace, not a reinvention.

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (1/2): Baker's leveraged $4B-scale bet to combine viagogo and StubHub, and his decision to persist through COVID rather than sell, show conviction [4]. Those bets, however, have aimed at scale and market power rather than at serving a Just Cause.

investment_thesis: StubHub is the scale leader in secondary ticketing, with accelerating 2026 growth: Q2 revenue rose 33% to $573.1M, GMS hit a record $3.1B, Q2 net income was $14.6M with an 18% adjusted EBITDA margin, and full-year GMS guidance was raised to $10.1-10.3B [1][6]. At $5.78 the stock trades at ~9.5x forward earnings, near its 52-week low [2].
thesis_continued: The bear case rests on governance and durability. A founder-controlled share structure, a $10M FTC fee settlement, and very weak employee sentiment weigh on the qualitative scores. World Cup-boosted 2026 comparisons will be hard to repeat in 2027, and trailing GAAP metrics remain deeply negative after the $1.9B FY2025 loss [3][4][5][7]. STUB is a WATCH for IOWN.
key_catalysts: Q3 2026 results and delivery against the raised $10.1-10.3B 2026 GMS guidance [6]
Sustained GAAP profitability after Q2 2026's $14.6M net income, moving trailing ROE and margins toward positive [1]
Growth of direct issuance partnerships with teams and venues [6]
key_risks: Regulatory scrutiny of ticket fees and resale (April 2026 FTC $10M settlement; state all-in pricing laws) [7]
Tough 2027 comparisons after the World Cup-driven 2026 GMS surge [6]
Controlled-company governance: the founder-CEO holds more than 50% of the voting power, with key-person risk [4]
Low employee trust and high turnover (Glassdoor 2.4/5, 24% CEO approval) [5]
